cha-com-ha-noi.name: Hanoi Chả Cốm (Young Rice Pork Patties)
cha-com-ha-noi.description: Pork and Vietnamese pork paste are mixed with fragrant young rice flakes, shaped into patties, briefly steamed and fried until lightly golden. This Bếp Việt home adaptation keeps the rice tender and aromatic.
cha-com-ha-noi.finished_dish: Lightly golden patties with fragrant young rice flakes and a moist, tender center; serve hot with rice, noodles or herbs.
cha-com-ha-noi.excerpt: Lightly golden patties with fragrant young rice flakes and a moist, tender center; serve hot with rice, noodles or herbs.
cha-com-ha-noi.serving: Serve the patties hot with steamed rice, vermicelli or fresh herbs. Pickled vegetables help balance the richness.
tips: If using dried rice flakes, soften with a little warm water first.
Brief steaming helps the patties hold their shape; fry over medium heat until the pork is cooked through.
Too much egg can make the mixture loose.
cha-com-ha-noi.tip: If using dried rice flakes, soften with a little warm water first.
cha-com-ha-noi.image_alt: Lightly golden Hanoi chả cốm pork patties with green young rice flakes.

ingredients.name: Ground pork
ingredients.notes: Pork shoulder with a little fat.

ingredients.name: Lotus leaf
ingredients.notes: Line the steamer; parchment also works.

preparation_steps.instruction: If needed, quickly rinse and drain fresh rice flakes. For dried flakes, sprinkle with warm water and rest 10 minutes until soft but not mushy.
Mix the pork, pork paste, shallot, fish sauce, sugar and pepper. Cover and chill for 10 minutes.
Lightly beat the egg, mix with the rice flakes and rest for 3–5 minutes.

cooking_steps.instruction: Fold the rice flakes into the pork and shape into 1.5 cm patties. Line a steamer with lotus leaf and brush lightly with oil.
Steam for 5–7 minutes until set, then remove and let excess steam dissipate.
Fry in batches over medium heat, turning until lightly golden and cooked through. Drain.

cha-com-ha-noi.time_note: Fry in small batches; timing depends on patty thickness.

ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-xu-quang.name: Quảng-Style Steamed Scad with Rice-Paper Rolls
ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-xu-quang.serving_basis: 4 servings of steamed fish with wrapping greens, rice paper and dipping sauce.
ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-xu-quang.description: Small scad are steamed with scallion, lemongrass and chili, then wrapped with cassava rice paper, tender water spinach and herbs. A little filtered steaming liquid can enrich the dipping sauce in this central-coast meal.
ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-xu-quang.finished_dish: Just-cooked sweet fish wrapped with crisp greens and flexible rice paper, served with tangy garlic-chili sauce.
ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-xu-quang.excerpt: Just-cooked sweet fish wrapped with crisp greens and flexible rice paper, served with tangy garlic-chili sauce.
ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-xu-quang.serving: Serve the hot fish with rice paper, greens and garlic-chili fish sauce. Wrap with herbs; add toasted rice crackers for crunch if desired.
tips: Choose small, firm fish with clear eyes; clean and dry thoroughly.
Avoid over-steaming; timing depends on fish size and the steamer.
Strain any steaming liquid used in the dip and season gradually.
ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-xu-quang.tip: Choose small, firm fish with clear eyes; clean and dry thoroughly.
ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-xu-quang.image_alt: Steamed scad with lemongrass, water spinach and rice-paper wraps, Quảng style.

preparation_steps.instruction: Scale and gut the fish, rub lightly with salt, rinse and pat dry.
Rinse the lemongrass, scallions and wrapping greens; drain well. Cut the cucumber into batons.
Mix fish sauce, water, sugar, lime and garlic; taste and adjust.

cooking_steps.instruction: Arrange lemongrass and shallot on a steaming plate, add the fish, scallions, pepper and chili.
Set the plate in the steamer once the water boils; steam small fish 12–15 minutes until opaque and flaky.
Serve hot with greens and rice paper. Briefly moisten each sheet, wrap fish and herbs, then dip.

ca-nuc-hap-cuon-banh-trang-xu-quang.time_note: The 12–15 minute guide suits small fish; larger fish need longer until cooked through.

bun-kiem-chay-mien-tay.name: Southern Vietnamese Vegetarian Bún Kiểm
bun-kiem-chay-mien-tay.serving_basis: 4 bowls of bún kiểm with vegetables in coconut broth.
bun-kiem-chay-mien-tay.description: A Southern Vietnamese noodle dish with root vegetables, pumpkin, just-ripe plantain, tofu and bean-curd sheets in vegetable broth enriched with coconut milk. This Bếp Việt version is served as a light soup with rice vermicelli.
bun-kiem-chay-mien-tay.finished_dish: A lightly thickened coconut broth with naturally sweet vegetables; the roots, pumpkin and tofu stay tender but hold their shape.
bun-kiem-chay-mien-tay.excerpt: A lightly thickened coconut broth with naturally sweet vegetables; the roots, pumpkin and tofu stay tender but hold their shape.
bun-kiem-chay-mien-tay.serving: Divide noodles among bowls and ladle over vegetables and broth. Top with peanuts and herbs; serve hot.
tips: Soak bean-curd sheets and mushrooms until soft, then drain well.
Add pumpkin and plantain after firmer roots so the vegetables keep their shape.
Keep the heat low after adding coconut milk and avoid a vigorous boil.
bun-kiem-chay-mien-tay.tip: Soak bean-curd sheets and mushrooms until soft, then drain well.
bun-kiem-chay-mien-tay.image_alt: Vegetarian bún kiểm with vegetables, tofu, bean-curd sheets and coconut broth.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning
ingredients.notes: Check label for a strict vegetarian diet.

preparation_steps.instruction: Soak bean-curd sheets and mushrooms until soft; drain. Wash, peel and cut the vegetables.
Briefly pan-sear sweet potato and taro in a little oil to set the surfaces.
Rinse and drain noodles and herbs; crush the peanuts.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat oil, stir the roots and mushrooms, then add vegetable stock and peanuts. Simmer until nearly tender.
Add pumpkin, plantain, tofu and bean-curd sheets; simmer gently for 10–12 minutes.
Lower the heat, add coconut milk, salt, sugar and vegetarian seasoning. Cook gently 3–4 minutes without boiling hard.
Blanch and divide the noodles into bowls. Ladle over the broth and top with peanuts and herbs.

bun-kiem-chay-mien-tay.time_note: Root-vegetable timing depends on size; cut evenly so pieces soften without breaking apart.

bo-nhung-giam.name: Vietnamese Beef Hotpot with Coconut Vinegar (Bò Nhúng Giấm)
bo-nhung-giam.serving_basis: 4 shared servings with dipping broth, beef, noodles, greens and rice paper.
bo-nhung-giam.description: Thin beef is dipped in coconut water broth with rice vinegar, lemongrass, onion and pineapple, then wrapped with vermicelli and vegetables in rice paper and served with mắm nêm. Its bright sweet-sour broth makes a convivial meal.
bo-nhung-giam.finished_dish: A fragrant pineapple and lemongrass broth, gently sweet and sour; wrap just-cooked beef with herbs and noodles, then dip in mắm nêm.
bo-nhung-giam.excerpt: A fragrant pineapple and lemongrass broth, gently sweet and sour; wrap just-cooked beef with herbs and noodles, then dip in mắm nêm.
bo-nhung-giam.serving: Keep the broth at a gentle simmer. Dip beef until cooked, wrap with vermicelli and vegetables in rice paper, and serve with pineapple mắm nêm.
tips: Slice beef across the grain and keep it chilled until serving.
Add vinegar gradually so the broth is bright rather than harsh.
Use separate utensils for raw and cooked meat; do not leave raw meat at room temperature.
bo-nhung-giam.tip: Slice beef across the grain and keep it chilled until serving.
bo-nhung-giam.image_alt: Beef vinegar hotpot with thin beef, pineapple, wrapping greens, rice paper and mắm nêm.

ingredients.name: Pineapple
ingredients.notes: Part for broth, part for serving.

ingredients.name: Fermented anchovy dipping sauce
ingredients.notes: Prepare as directed on the label.

ingredients.name: Green banana
ingredients.notes: Thinly slice and soak in lemon water.

preparation_steps.instruction: Slice beef across the grain, arrange on a plate and refrigerate. Wash greens; cut cucumber, green banana and pineapple.
Bruise lemongrass and slice onion. Divide pineapple for broth, dip and wraps.
Mix mắm nêm with minced pineapple, garlic, chili, sugar and a little water; adjust to taste.

cooking_steps.instruction: Add coconut water, plain water, lemongrass, onion and broth pineapple; simmer 8–10 minutes.
Gradually add vinegar; season with sugar and salt for a gentle sweet-sour taste. Keep at a light simmer.
Serve with beef, noodles, greens and rice paper. Dip each slice until cooked, wrap with noodles and vegetables, and serve with mắm nêm.

bo-nhung-giam.time_note: Prep time excludes eating at the table; keep the broth gently simmering so the beef stays tender.

nem-thinh-chay.name: Vietnamese Vegetarian Nem Thính (Mushroom and Toasted Rice Salad)
nem-thinh-chay.serving_basis: 4 servings to wrap with greens or enjoy with noodles and rice paper.
nem-thinh-chay.description: King oyster mushrooms are cut into strands, blanched and fried until springy, then tossed with glass noodles, toasted rice powder and lime leaves. This Bếp Việt version uses vegetarian seasoning and a plant-based dip with fresh greens.
nem-thinh-chay.finished_dish: Springy mushroom strands coated in nutty toasted rice powder, with soft glass noodles and fragrant lime leaf; wrap in greens or serve with vermicelli.
nem-thinh-chay.excerpt: Springy mushroom strands coated in nutty toasted rice powder, with soft glass noodles and fragrant lime leaf; wrap in greens or serve with vermicelli.
nem-thinh-chay.serving: Serve with wild fig leaves, perilla, lettuce, rice paper and vermicelli, alongside sweet-sour vegetarian dipping sauce or diluted soy sauce.
tips: Squeeze mushrooms dry after blanching to reduce oil splatter and help the rice powder coat evenly.
Cool mushrooms slightly before adding the powder so the mixture does not become damp and clumpy.
For a fully vegetarian meal, check seasonings, dipping sauce and rice paper for animal ingredients.
nem-thinh-chay.tip: Squeeze mushrooms dry after blanching to reduce oil splatter and help the rice powder coat evenly.
nem-thinh-chay.image_alt: Vegetarian nem thính with king oyster mushrooms, glass noodles, toasted rice powder and herbs.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning
ingredients.notes: Check the label for strict vegetarian diets.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying; most oil is not absorbed.

preparation_steps.instruction: Rinse mushrooms, slice lengthwise and cut into strands. Soak glass noodles, briefly blanch, rinse cool and cut into 5–6 cm lengths.
Shred lime leaves and chili. Wash wild fig leaves and herbs, then drain thoroughly.
Mix soy sauce with water, lime and sugar; adjust the sweet-sour balance.

cooking_steps.instruction: Blanch mushrooms for about 1 minute, rinse cool and squeeze very dry in a clean towel.
Fry mushrooms in small batches until springy and lightly golden. Drain and cool slightly.
Toss mushrooms and noodles with salt, vegetarian seasoning, pepper, chili and lime leaves. Add rice powder gradually and mix gently.
Serve with wild fig leaves, herbs, vermicelli and rice paper with sweet-sour soy dip.

nem-thinh-chay.time_note: Rice powder absorbs moisture quickly; add gradually just before serving to keep the mixture loose.
